title: Sex-dependent seasonal variation in body-size-adjusted cheliped dimensions of Tubuca paradussumieri (Bott, 1973) (Decapoda: Brachyura: Ocypodidae)
content:
Abstract
Sexual dimorphism of the chelipeds is a defining feature of fiddler crabs, but the extent to which the male-female contrast varies between seasons remains poorly understood in Tubuca paradussumieri (Bott, 1973). We examined body-size-adjusted variation in four cheliped dimensions of 1,158 individuals collected monthly for 12 months from six mangrove sites in southwestern Vietnam. Linear mixed-effects models included mean carapace width, carapace-width asymmetry, sex, season, and the sex × season interaction as fixed effects, with sampling region included as a random effect. Body size was positively associated with all four dimensions (P < 0.001), whereas carapace-width asymmetry had only a small effect on pollex width. After accounting for body size, males had larger minimum and maximum manus widths, pollex width, and dactyl width than females (P < 0.001). Seasonal main effects were trait-specific: maximum manus width and pollex width were greater in the wet season, whereas minimum manus width and dactyl width did not differ significantly between seasons. The sex × season interaction was significant for all traits (P < 0.05), with negative coefficients indicating that the male-female difference was smaller in the wet season than in the dry season. Fixed effects explained 75.8–87.4% of the variation, and the full models explained 77.0–87.6%. These results show that seasonal variation was not uniform across cheliped components; instead, seasonal context modified the magnitude of sexual dimorphism after body size was taken into account.
